name: UK Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024
description: Statutory rules covering the UK DMCC Act 2024 mandatory pre-renewal disclosure schedules and 14-day cooling-off rights for UK consumers.

rules.title: Mandatory Pre-Renewal Reminder Schedule

statute.title: Subscription Contracts — Pre-Renewal Reminders
statute.plainExplanation: The UK DMCC Act 2024 requires traders to provide timely, conspicuous reminder notices before a subscription automatically renews or converts from a trial.

rules.explanation: The terms state or imply that the subscription will auto-renew without mandatory pre-renewal reminder notices sent to you.
rules.recommendation: Verify that the trader has committed to sending advance renewal reminders before charges recur. Under UK law, failure to send reminders renders renewal unenforceable.

rules.title: 14-Day Statutory Cooling-Off Rights Obstruction

statute.code: UK DMCC Act 2024, Part 2, Chapter 1 (Cancellation Rights)
statute.title: 14-Day Subscription Cooling-Off Rights
statute.plainExplanation: UK consumers possess an unwaivable statutory right to cancel a subscription contract within a 14-day cooling-off window at inception and upon material renewal.

rules.explanation: The contract denies, restricts, or claims to waive your statutory 14-day cooling-off cancellation rights.
rules.recommendation: Do not waive cooling-off cancellation rights. UK law prohibits traders from excluding statutory 14-day withdrawal windows for consumer subscriptions.

rules.title: Unilateral Variation of Material Subscription Terms

statute.title: Unfair Contract Terms — Unilateral Variations
statute.plainExplanation: Terms granting traders unlimited unilateral discretion to alter subscription pricing, deliverables, or material specifications without consumer opt-out are presumptively unfair.

rules.explanation: The contract reserves unrestricted powers to alter prices or core subscription terms unilaterally without reasonable advance notice.
rules.recommendation: Under the UK Consumer Rights Act 2015, unfair price variation clauses are legally unenforceable against consumer subscribers.
